context: The input choices = [1, 2, 3] has distinct elements at indices 0, 1, and 2. Each element can appear only once in a given permutation. The variable state holds the current prefix. The Boolean array selected records, by input index, whether each element has been chosen on the current path.
description: The restriction in selected applies only to the current recursive path. Skip marked indices on the way down and clear each mark when backtracking from that choice. Choosing 1 does not permanently disable it. Other permutation branches can still use it.

The figure fully expands only the path [] → [1] → [1, 3] → [1, 3, 2]. Pruning marks indicate repeated choices that the search never enters. For example, [1, 1] would select element 1 at index 0 a second time after prefix [1]. Ellipses indicate valid branches whose continuations are omitted. The table groups the choice restrictions, pruned branches, and omitted continuations by prefix.

frames.explanation: The highlighted path produces the permutation [1, 3, 2].
